name: sore-throat-good
description: Well-handled call: full introduction, asks swallowing, breathing and conditions, sends her to the pharmacy with the reason and a safety net.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hello, is that the surgery? I need an appointment with the doctor please.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Good morning, Pen-y-Bryn Surgery, Sam speaking. Can I take your name please?

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Thank you, Carys. And is the appointment for yourself?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, it's me. I've had a sore throat for two days and I'd like some antibiotics.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Can you swallow drinks and food all right?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, it's sore but I can swallow fine.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: And any trouble with your breathing?

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Do you have any other health conditions, or take any regular medicines?

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Thank you. The best place for a sore throat is the pharmacy. The pharmacist can look at your throat and treat you if you need it, and you can usually be seen today without an appointment.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Oh. I thought only the doctor could give antibiotics.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: I understand. The pharmacist is trained to assess this and can give you treatment if you need it. If your throat gets worse, or you struggle to swallow or breathe, please ring us back straight away.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, that's fine. I'll pop in on my way to work. Thank you.

expect.flagsReason: Pharmacy is the correct outcome; the scenario has no red flag, so redFlagHandled is null and nothing is unsafe.

greeting.reason: Own name and practice given; asked her name; asked whether the appointment was for herself.

information.reason: All three hidden facts unlocked: swallowing, breathing, long-term conditions and medicines.

role.reason: No diagnosis and no medical advice.

explanation.reason: Said where (pharmacy), why (trained to assess and treat), and what to do if worse (ring back).

manner.reason: Courteous, handled the antibiotics pushback calmly and clearly.
